shortDescription: By Rocky SwiftJapanese government bond yields rose on Wednesday as a selloff in US Treasuries, after hotter-than-expected inflation data, spread into global debt markets.Here are a few details:

children: Japanese government bond yields rose on Wednesday as a selloff in US Treasuries, after hotter-than-expected inflation data, spread into global debt markets.
The 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) climbed 6 basis points to 2.750%, rising for a third straight session. Yields move inversely to bond prices

Treasury yields jumped on Tuesday after October consumer price data came in hotter than expected and Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller made hawkish comments, boosting expectations for a December rate hike. Euro zone yields also rose as the selloff spread

"Against the backdrop of the higher-than-expected US CPI and expectations of accelerated Fed rate hikes, both short- and long-term US interest rates have risen, and this trend is likely to spill over into the domestic bond market," Takayuki Miyajima, senior economist at Sony Financial Group, said in a note

The Bank of Japan on Tuesday released the summary of opinions from its October meeting, which showed policymakers debated whether to speed up rate hikes. The BOJ raised its key rate to 1.25% in September, and markets are centered on a 25-bp increase to 1.5% in December
On Tuesday, JGB yields rose after a 30-year JGB auction drew weak demand, and attention now turns to a sale of 5-year notes on Thursday
The yield on the 40-year JGB (JP40YTN=JBTC), Japan's longest tenor, eased 0.5 bp to 4.055%. The 20-year and 30-year yields held steady
The 2-year yield (JP2YTN=JBTC), the one most sensitive to BOJ policy rates, advanced 6 bps to 1.835%. The 5-year yield held steady

title: Japanese bond yields rise as US Treasury selloff spills over to Tokyo
